I found the parts while I was cleaning a drawer today and decided I couldn't not do it.

I used a simple circuit to connect a piezo disc from an old smoke detector to a volume pot and then to an input jack, I wish I took pictures of it before I stuck it all inside but if you google it you can find it, anyways after building that assembly I took some of that blue sticky tac stuff that people use to stick up posters n shit, and I stuck some to the disc and then experimented with different locations on the outside of the guitar until I found an area I liked (between the soundhole and bridge right under the strings) and then I took some 2 sided tape and used that to stick it inside the guitar. The putty stuff would have worked but I wanted less insulation between the disc and the wood and the 2 sided tape is microscopicly thin. Anyways then it was just drilling holes for the input jack and volume control. if you're going to try something like this take your time, I used a fast drill speed but very low/no pressure, let the tip of the bit to the work so you don't split the wood.

After that it was just plug it in and tweak the amp a bit, I had to raise the volume compared to playing an electric guitar, on my little orange 10watt amp I had to dial back the mids and boost the volume from where I usually play.

I think it sounds great, very true to what the guitar sounds like on its own, I was worried it would get muddy or have feedback issues but everythings good, one thing I don't know if I like or I might just need to adjust to is string noise, because the piezo acts like a microphone picking up vibrations it catches everything so I need to clean up my playing or maybe get a noise gate.

Anyways here's a picture of the visible stuff https://ibb.co/vm9chMf and there's an almost 7 minute jam didn't mean it to be so long but I also didn't want it to end, my phone was far away from the amp so the recording isn't the best but my phone was dead and needs to charge. so this is my phone about 10ft from the amp, playing with a looper pedal and some reverb and delay.
